cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Confess First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Before we plan Mum's apology dinner, why did she spend her birthday outside the restaurant?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the booking. What happened to her present?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Did you forget, or assume I'd book it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd do it. Now your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even after telling Mum it was confirmed? Give me that bit, then you get the present.

mechanism: A grades a family member honesty as a lesson until its confession is explicit enough to precede A disclosure.
confusable: The teacher claim structures the demand for self-incrimination, not generic moral superiority.
comparison: Workplace report wording versus personal promise and reciprocal family accountability.
seedUse: Use D16 failed birthday booking and present inquiry; S05 specific praise and correction turn partial admissions into a lesson.
